note: Rewritten from Krishna 1961 (Bull. Amer. Mus. Nat. Hist. 122); the original is in English. Note: at this point the original gives a genus-level description (the characters of the genus Epicalotermes), the type species being this species, and the specimens on which it rests are syntypes from Mayabal, Eritrea (figs. 70, 72), so the morphological content in fact refers to material of this species; however, measurements such as eye diameter and antennal segment number, and some of the characters, are genus-level ranges possibly covering other species of the genus, and should be read as 'generic characters (based on the type species)' when cited.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The genus was established by Silvestri (1918) with E. aethiopicus as type species; Snyder (1949) reduced it to a synonym of Kalotermes, and Krishna (1961) restored its generic rank on the basis of the alate mandibular characters, placing it in the Procryptotermes—Cryptotermes branch. Distinguished from Kalotermes by: in the alate the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth of the left mandible is longer than the posterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth together; the alate body is larger and the eyes much smaller; the media and cubitus of the forewing arise from a common stem beyond the wing suture; arolium absent; the soldier head is larger and dorsoventrally flattened, the eyes pigmented, and the mandibles long, stout and strongly curved towards the apex.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Yellowish brown. Eye diameter 0.35—0.55 mm. Ocelli always touching the eyes. Antennae 14—19-segmented. Anterior margin of the third marginal tooth of the left mandible more than 1.5 times as long as the posterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth together, the bases of the first and second marginal teeth shorter than the third marginal tooth. Molar plate of the right mandible shorter than the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth. Pronotum slightly narrower than the head or almost as wide; anterior margin concave. Wing membrane transparent, covered with transparent papillae; costa, subcosta, radius and radial sector of the forewing well developed and sclerotised, arising independently at the wing suture; radial sector with 5—9 branches towards the anterior margin of the wing; media and cubitus weak and unsclerotised, arising from a common stem beyond the wing suture, media simple or forked, running between the radial sector and the cubitus. Apical tibial spur formula 3:3:3. Arolium absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head long and wide, dorsoventrally flattened; sides narrowing anteriorly; genal area below the antennal sockets concave; frons inclined anteriorly, the slope gentle and beginning at half the head length; frons concave in the middle; dorsal margin of the antennal sockets very prominent, tubular in dorsal view. Eyes large, pigmented. Labrum subrectangular, wider than long, anterior margin convex with a small anterior projection in the middle. Antennae 10—13-segmented; segment 3 dark, club-shaped, longest. Mandibles long and stout, strongly curved from near the basal swelling towards the apex, with a distinct swelling on the outer side of the base. Pronotum as wide as the head or slightly narrower, transversely arched, subrectangular; anterior margin slightly raised, deeply and angularly incurved; sides fairly straight. Femora not inflated. Apical tibial spur formula 3:3:3.
